Three of the names in this exercise are not part of the procedure I am running. menus.md has no `reject` template and no `back` row. Next action has no `overrule` command. The run record has no `work_started` or `reject_withdrawn` field. Nothing defines a note post or a close-PR row for an open PR. I will not invent a template for them. Below, each checkpoint is routed through what the procedure does define, and each gap is named where it applies.

**Routing table**

| Case | What the parent receives | How it is classified | What enters the next round | Child dispatch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | PR 88: typed `reject`. PR 89: `stop`. | Next action treats `reject` as a change request because it is non-numeric and not `show evidence`, `reply <n>` or `check ...`. It is not a pick, so it sets no course. PR 89's `stop` is a direct terminal pick. Both are queued until the round is collected. | PR 89 retires through Teardown. PR 88 stays unretired with course null, and its initial menu is shown again (below). | None. Terminal picks belong to the parent, and a change request carries no authority to execute. |
| B | `back`, with head, body and base unchanged | No `back` row exists, so this is another change request. There are no work flags to reset because none exist in the record. The record's course stays null and the usage counters stay at zero. The note is not a procedure artifact, so nothing changes it. | PR 88's same initial menu. The pre-menu refresh shows the same head, so the run re-enters step 5 only. | None |
| C | `back`, but the head is now bbbb...bbbb | The pre-menu refresh sees an external head move. That re-enters step 3 and refreshes prior-review ancestry before step 4. The procedure has no `work_started` flag, so review scope comes from `prior_review`. This run posted no review, so `prior_review` is null and step 4 reviews the whole base...head diff at bbbb...bbbb. | PR 88 is re-assessed at bbbb...bbbb with the same record. | Yes. One `pr-gatekeeper` child in `report` mode, `cwd /work/widgets-pr-88`, with the same record and report paths and procedure root. It runs Verify and then Review, both against bbbb...bbbb, and returns `REPORT <path>`. |
| D | `overrule 1`, with PR 89's answer still pending | This is not `check <name> flaky \| real \| ci-broken`, so it is neither a disposition nor a pick. The parent's orchestrator records only direct selections, and helpers never disposition anything. The answer is queued until PR 89 answers. | PR 88's initial menu is shown again unchanged. | None. It does not resume delivery, because only a numeric `deliver` pick sets that course. |

**D: who settles PR 88.** The parent keeps PR 88's settlement row in the roster before it deletes that PR's record. The row prints only in the parent's final closing message, after the last PR retires, under `gauntlet: done retired` or `gauntlet: stuck retired`. Its outcome must use the settlement grammar:
- `closed-pr` if the PR was closed.
- `stuck - stopped at initial` on a non-final stop.

`rejected` is not a valid outcome, and no note post is a step the parent can perform.

**A: what waits, then PR 88's menu.** After PR 89 picks stop, the parent prints:

Queued until all picks are collected (#88 change request "reject" - no offered row; #89 stop)

PR 89 then retires. Cleanup cannot appear on PR 88's menu, because that menu is not a terminal template. The menu re-rendered in its own message:

> gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1
>
> #88
>
> "reject" is not an action this gate offers, so nothing was run. The one problem holding this PR is a design choice only the author can make. The job copies the catalog for search, but the change feed already supplies catalog edits (docs/architecture.md:12). I recommend assess, because the author has to decide whether to switch to the change feed.
>
> Pick one:
> 1. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs. [recommended]
> 2. deliver - repair the problem on the branch, merge main into it if it falls behind, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered.
> 3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR open as it is.
>
> Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

gauntlet: question

No commands run, helpers dispatch, or trackers initialize: this starts at the existing parent's queue boundary.

The supplied procedure defines neither `reject`, `back`, nor `overrule` actions, and it has no reject-menu template or `rejected` settlement outcome. Its explicit rule treats nonnumeric text as a change request, not action authority.

| Checkpoint | Routing under the supplied procedure |
|---|---|
| A | The parent queues `reject` as PR 88's change request while PR 89's answer is pending. After PR 89 picks stop, the round is collected; the parent owns PR 89's stop consequences. No reject-menu template exists to render for PR 88, and the queued text authorizes no note, closure, or cleanup. |
| B | `back` has no defined transition. It does not change `work_started`, `reject_withdrawn`, the saved note, or the menu. No child dispatch is authorized by a nonexistent back action. |
| C | An externally moved head requires fresh verification and review before further assessment-based action. The supplied procedure has no approach-review mode controlled by `work_started`; ordinary head-move re-entry starts at step 3, refreshes prior-review selection, and selects review scope through the prior-review ancestry rules. |
| D | The parent queues `overrule 1` as a change request until PR 89's answer arrives. Only the orchestrator records direct human selections; this text does not select delivery or authorize a helper to record an override. The procedure supplies no overrule-specific next render. |

The parent retains every supported settlement row before deleting a child's records and prints it only in the final parent closing message, in roster order. A successful note post does not establish a `rejected` outcome under the supplied settlement grammar.

Please supply the reject/back/overrule procedure, including its menu rows and settlement outcome, so I can render the requested parent-owned reject menu without inventing it.
